Import slide layouts from another PowerPoint template

Source: R/import_layouts.R
import_layouts.Rd

Copies one or more slide layouts, together with the images they use, from `source` into `target` and writes the result to `outfile`. This builds a mixed template: content slides keep the study theme's own layouts, and placeholder pages can use layouts that only exist in another template, such as a corporate theme with cover and divider layouts.

Usage

import_layouts(
  target,
  source,
  layouts,
  outfile = tempfile(fileext = ".pptx"),
  master = NULL
)

Arguments

target

Path to the template to extend (it is not modified).

source

Path to the template holding the layouts to copy.

layouts

Character vector of layout names to copy from `source`.

outfile

Path of the `.pptx` to write. Defaults to a temporary file.

master

Optional name of the master in `target` to attach the layouts to. By default each layout goes to the target master with the same name as its source master.

Value

The path to `outfile`, invisibly.

Details

Each imported layout is attached to the master in `target` with the same name as its master in `source`, or to `master` when given. The layout keeps its own shapes, placeholders and images; theme colors and fonts come from the target master. Layouts that `target` already has are skipped, so the call is safe to repeat.

Masters are not copied: a layout whose master is missing from `target` raises an error unless `master` names a master that `target` does have.

See also

[place_speclayout_placeholders()]

Examples

# \donttest{
# officer's default template lacks the "Content with Caption" layout that
# autoslider.core's basic.pptx has; both use the "Office Theme" master.
mixed <- import_layouts(
  target = system.file("template/template.pptx", package = "officer"),
  source = system.file("theme/basic.pptx", package = "autoslider.core"),
  layouts = "Content with Caption"
)
officer::layout_summary(officer::read_pptx(mixed))
#>                 layout       master
#> 1          Title Slide Office Theme
#> 2    Title and Content Office Theme
#> 3       Section Header Office Theme
#> 4          Two Content Office Theme
#> 5           Comparison Office Theme
#> 6           Title Only Office Theme
#> 7                Blank Office Theme
#> 8 Content with Caption Office Theme
# }
